Corrected: the simple restricted Lie algebras are not, up to finitely many low-characteristic exceptions, those of the simple algebraic groups: in every characteristic p ≥ 3 the Witt algebra W(1) = Der(k[x]/(x^p)), of dimension p, is simple and restricted, and the Cartan-type families W, S, H, K are infinite (Kostrikin–Shafarevich, Block–Wilson, Premet–Strade; Melikian algebras in characteristic 5). Probably the lecturer's oral simplification (the classification was open in 1973); flagged uncertain. Not formalised: restricted Lie algebras of Cartan type are not in Mathlib.

correction.old: Simple restricted $p$-Lie algebras over an algebraically closed field: the commutative ones ($\alpha_p$, $\mu_p$), and otherwise (finitely many exceptions in low characteristic) the Lie algebras of the simple algebraic groups of the Cartan–Killing types. (Information in SGA 3.)
correction.new: Simple restricted $p$-Lie algebras over an algebraically closed field: the commutative ones ($\alpha_p$, $\mu_p$), and otherwise the classical ones, from the simple algebraic groups of the Cartan–Killing types, and those of Cartan type ($W,S,H,K$, e.g. the Witt algebra of dimension $p$), with further ones in characteristic $\le5$. (Information in SGA 3.)
